مِضْخَمٌ , as an epithet applied to a chief, or lord, (tropical:) Noble, and portly, or corpulent; (K, TA;) as also ↓ ضَخْمٌ . (TA.) ―
-b2- And, applied to a man, (TA,) (tropical:) Vehement in dashing himself against another; and in striking, or beating. (K, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
